fix: what I have already explained at some length
reason: διὰ πλειόνων means 'at greater length', not 'more than once'.
εἰ καί τις ἄλλος is 'if anyone ever did': he was supremely experienced, which is the point of καίτοι γε.

fix: When the party led by Agepolis entered
reason: Greek Ἁγέπολις; use corpus spelling Agepolis (Books 28, 29.10), not Hegesipolis or Hagepolis.

fix: what the men around Agepolis said
reason: Same envoy Ἁγέπολις; corpus spelling Agepolis.

fix: whose name was not even known before
reason: οὐδ᾽ ὄνομα … ἦν γνώριμον is a full negation; 'scarcely' weakens it. Minimal wording change.
γάρ justifies the restriction 'in earlier times' (Antiochus IV was generous); 'although' renders that logic correctly. No inversion.
ἐξήρτυε (imperfect of ἐξαρτύω) means 'was fitting out, preparing' war, not 'resumed'.

fix: the answer that Agepolis and his colleagues had obtained
reason: Ἁγέπολις, the Rhodian envoy of 29.19, not the Spartan name Agesipolis; corpus spelling Agepolis.

fix: and they put every hope to the test.
reason: πάσας ἐξήλεγχον τὰς ἐλπίδας: they tried every hope (did not despair); 'disappointed all expectations' inverts the sense.
Not a lacuna: anacoluthon, the verb is resumed by οἷς ἅπασιν … ἀπήντησε after the parenthesis. 'dealt with' bridges it legitimately.

fix: having been compelled to fight three wars against them
reason: πολεμεῖν αὐτοῖς: dative of the opponents, so wars against the Lycians/Carians, not wars 'over' the regions.
'alone' is added. ἐκ πάντων could mean 'from every indication' or 'out of all men'; the translator should choose.
